title: Redwood February 2026 All-Hands
summary: Monthly company all-hands. CEO Maya opened with high-level business metrics and a reminder on mission. CTO Carlos presented runtime and reliability improvements (KV cache, batching) and upcoming Private deployment milestones. Product reviewed roadmap priorities: Dedicated autoscaling, cost optimization toolkit, and rollout of new observability dashboards. Sales highlighted several enterprise POCs and renewals. Leadership announced two senior hires and an org tweak in platform. Session closed with Q&A and follow-ups assigned.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-05
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Maya J, Carlos R, Aisha P, Leo K, Renee T, Tom B, company-wide

[00:00] Maya: Okay hi everyone, uh thanks for joining the February all-hands. Happy to see so many of you on. We'll kick off with a quick business update then Carlos will walk through some infra and reliability stuff, Aisha will do product roadmap, Renee will cover sales highlights and then we'll do q&a.

[00:22] Maya: High level — Q1 targets look healthy, we're tracking slightly ahead of plan on ARR growth, we closed three mid-market deals last month and we have two enterprise POCs in flight that look promising. I want to reiterate our thesis — serving-first, developer-first — keep focusing on predictable inference economics.

[00:45] Maya: There was an incident last week impacting a small set of Dedicated customers, I asked Carlos to talk through root cause and next steps. But first, hiring — we've hired Priya Kapoor as Director of Product Marketing and we have two senior infra hires joining next month. Welcome all.

[01:10] Carlos: Hi all, Carlos here. Quick on the incident — summary: mis-routed KV cache invalidation after a config change led to degraded latency for a subset of requests on one pool. It was not a data breach, but customer experience was impacted. We rolled back the change, increased telemetry, and added a safety check in the rollout pipeline. Tom's team is owning the postmortem doc.

[01:40] Carlos: Tech details — the problem was a combination of optimistic cache invalidation with a new kernel selection heuristic. Essentially for some model variants the runtime chose an incompatible kernel path which resulted in higher memory churn and GC-like pauses on the hosts. We're improving our kernel selection tests and adding a canary policy that routes a small percent to the new path with additional tracing.

[02:15] Tom: yeah and adding — the fix was fast, the rollback took about 12 minutes, we then throttled new deploys and ran a targeted benchmark. We'll publish the postmortem in #incidents in the next 48 hours.

[02:35] Carlos: Longer term, the KV prefix caching adjustments and batching improvements we've been rolling out should reduce tail latency substantially. Early numbers look like p95 down by ~18% on synthetic loads.

[03:00] Aisha: on roadmap — short term Q1 priorities: 1) Dedicated autoscaling (GA target Q2), 2) Redwood Optimize v1 (cost/perf toolkit) with recommendations and automated batching knobs, 3) Private deployment beta for EU customers, and 4) Observability: token-level cost and per-route dashboards. We're prioritizing those because they map directly to customer asks for predictability and cost controls.

[03:40] Aisha: Note on prioritization — we heard from several customers that Dedicated autoscale and predictable pricing are blockers for procurement. So we're moving capacity and pricing work up the queue.

[04:10] Leo: engineering notes — autoscale is implemented as a policy layer on top of the existing pool manager. We still need to finish elasticity tests (esp workload bursts), and validate pre-emption behavior across instance types. We'll run a stress test mid-February.

[04:35] Renee: Sales update — we have four POCs live: two for fin-tech, one for healthcare, one for an enterprise search customer. Deal team is asking for a short benchmarking artifact: end-to-end latency numbers and cost estimates for both hosted and dedicated. Also legal is pushing on data residency for the healthcare POC. We're coordinating with product on Private options.

[05:05] Renee: On renewals, we've got two smaller customers up in March that we're confident this year; upsell motion is picking up. There's some competitive pressure from LargeCloudAI on price but our SLOs + tooling have been resonating.

[05:30] Maya: quick reminder — for all public/partner mentions, check with comms; also please be mindful of embargoes on POC news.

[05:45] Employee (Q): any update on OKR cadence and how we measure success this quarter?

[05:50] Maya: we tightened the OKR rolls to focus on output metrics: p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, number of certified model variants, and enterprise ARR expansion. Managers will publish team-level metrics next week.

[06:10] Employee (Q): will Private GA be in EMEA only or global?

[06:15] Aisha: the beta will be EMEA-first due to some customer demand and region compliance, but plan is global GA — timeline depends on a couple of legal/KMS integrations.

[06:40] Employee (Q): what about SOC2/ISO and audit readiness?

[06:45] Leo: we're on track for SOC 2 Type II this quarter, ISO we expect later in the year. We're also adding finer-grained audit logs and exporting options for Dedicated/Private.

[07:05] Employee (Q): any change to hiring plans?

[07:10] Maya: we are actually expanding — we'll add 18 roles in Q1 across infra, product, and sales. People Ops will share the list.

[07:25] Carlos: I want to call out a small-but-important runtime improvement that shipped: KV cache hot-key mitigation. We saw a nasty tail effect in synthetic benchmarks; the mitigation routes hot prefixes to isolated workers which reduces noisy neighbor effects. Early tests show better stability for heavy prompt workloads.

[07:55] Tom: plus we shipped a small model compilation optimization that reduces peak memory on the 40B variants; helpful for Dedicated customers on mid-range GPUs. Expect small perf gains but meaningful cost savings for customers.

[08:20] Renee: customer ask — we should standardize a benchmarking spreadsheet to give to POCs. I'll work with Tom and Aisha on a template.

[08:35] Aisha: yep, we'll add that to the sales playbook; include recommended sequences, example prompts, and expected latency/cost ranges.

[08:50] Q&A rapid fire:
[08:52] Employee: what's the policy on external talks?

[08:55] Maya: we encourage talks but run them by comms first.

[09:02] Employee: is there a preferred region for new Dedicated customers?

[09:05] Leo: usually US-west for lowest latency to core infra, but we support EU regions and can discuss region-specific hardware if needed.

[09:20] Employee: any changes to PTO?

[09:22] Maya: no changes; we'll send a reminder about holiday scheduling shortly.

[09:35] Wrap-up:
[09:36] Maya: thanks everyone. Recap: incident postmortem, roadmap doc, hiring tracker and enterprise POC list are the immediate follow-ups. We'll do leadership office hours next week for deeper questions.

[09:52] Carlos: one last thing — if you see performance regressions on nightly runs, please tag #perf and @tom so we can triage quickly.

[10:00] Maya: meeting adjourned. Thanks all.
